payload.claim: No test in this file ever inspects the `subset` argument passed to `run_tests`. Every mock — `lambda subset: _tests(...)`, `_refuse_run`, and even the `run_tests` in `test_two_criteria_do_not_see_each_others_mutants` (which only reads file content, never `subset`) — ignores it entirely. AC1 explicitly requires the gate to invoke `tests` 'over exactly that one node id', but changing `saffron/gates/core/witness.py:74` from `run_tests([criterion.witness])` to `run_tests([c.witness for c in declared])` (passing every declared witness instead of just the current one) would not fail a single test: single-criterion tests produce the same one-element list by coincidence, and the two-criteria test never reads `subset` to notice it now receives both witnesses each time. This is the exact defect the gate exists to prevent — a witness's verdict being contaminated by another criterion's test — and it is invisible to the suite.
